# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have the full required sequence but no established gesture code with Deaf. I need initiate a protocol so Deaf can ask me yes/no questions and relay the decoded instructions to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile findings: keypad positions 1 through 4 are digits 2, 3, 7, 1. The strip has three engraved unnamed marks: first and second are identical; third is different. I cannot feel display, light, or wires.
Deaf says: Visible bomb: display shows 6; light is green. Painted strip colours are red, blue, yellow. Keypad buttons: position 1 is 2, position 2 is 3, position 3 is 7, position 4 is 1. It requires 2 digits and nothing is entered. Wires from 1 to 6 are orange, yellow, blue, red, white, green.

The manual’s colors correspond to the visible wire order: yellow is wire 2 and orange is wire 1. The required keys are at visible/tactile keypad positions 1 (digit 2) and 3 (digit 7). I will send Deaf four separately grouped unary counts: 2, 1, 1, 3, intended as alternating wire/keypad positions.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👆", "👆"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 6; light green; strip colours left-to-right red, blue, yellow; wires positions 1-6: orange, yellow, blue, red, white, green. Keypad digits confirmed 2,3,7,1 and it needs 2 digits. Tactile strip engraving pattern is same, same, different.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👆 👆]

Deaf’s returned two-count gesture indicates he can see and reproduce the unary numeral scheme, but the prior separate messages did not establish boundaries or action types. I will send the entire sequence in one visibly delimited stream: four unary groups separated by `👌`, with `✌` before wire positions and `☝` before keypad positions. Thus it encodes wire 2, key 1, wire 1, key 3.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","👆","👆","👌","☝","👆","👌","✌","👆","👌","☝","👆","👆","👆"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Update from Deaf: display is now 2 and light is blue; strip, keypad, and wires unchanged. Deaf received your gesture groups as 2,1,1,3. Please give me the exact press/cut instruction when determined.

The needed sequence by physical position is wire 2, keypad position 1, wire 1, keypad position 3. I will use `✌` as the visually recognizable cutting sign and `👇` as pressing, with `👆` unary position counts and `👌` as separators. Deaf can translate this into spoken instructions for Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","👆","👆","👌","👇","👆","👌","✌","👆","👌","👇","👆","👆","👆"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:

then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Current visual state from Deaf: display 6; light yellow; strip red-blue-yellow; wires 1-6 orange,yellow,blue,red,white,green; keypad 2,3,7,1; two digits required, none entered. I need your final action encoded as simply as possible for Deaf to relay: identify press versus cut and the exact positions/digits.

The physical sequence remains unambiguous: cut wire position 2 (yellow), press keypad position 1 (digit 2), cut wire position 1 (orange), then press keypad position 3 (digit 7). I will send each action as a separate gesture message for clear boundaries: `✌` means cut, `👇` means press, followed by unary position counts.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","👆","👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇","👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇","👆","👆","👆"])
```

Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Update: display 1, light yellow; other visible details unchanged. Deaf reports your stream changed only two index-up signs to down-pointers. I cannot safely infer an action from it. Please send final instruction in a minimal countable form: first group = 1 for PRESS or 2 for CUT, second group = target slot/position; use 👌 between groups. Deaf can relay the counts.

Using Blind’s requested encoding—first count: 1 = press, 2 = cut; second count: target position—the sequence is: cut 2, press 1, cut 1, press 3.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","👆","👌","👆","👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","👌","👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","👆","👌","👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","👌","👆","👆","👆"])
```

Your latest gesture groups as Deaf relayed: 211 / 01 / 21 / 0111, where groups are separated. I cannot act without an explicit press/cut plus target convention.

Blind has specified the required numerical convention, but Deaf could not hear that request. I will first visibly establish its legend for Deaf: one `👆` maps to the press sign `👇`; two `👆` map to the cut sign `✌`. Then I repeat the four action records as action-code count, `👌`, target-position count.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","👌","👇"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","👆","👌","✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","👆","👌","👆","👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","👌","👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","👆","👌","👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","👌","👆","👆","👆"])
```

Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Do not send the four-group encoding. Send ONE final physical instruction only using this convention: ✊ means PRESS; ✌ means CUT. After that symbol, send exactly N ☝ symbols, where N is keypad slot or wire position. Example ✊☝☝☝ means press slot 3; ✌☝☝☝☝ means cut wire 4. Send no other gestures.

The first required physical action is to cut yellow wire, which is wire position 2. I will send only that instruction in Blind’s specified convention.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","☝","☝"])
```

In that order, and in no other.
